record.title: CS/CS/HB 527 (2026): Mandatory Human Reviews of Insurance Claim Denials (passed House, died in Senate)
record.short_title: Florida HB 527 (2026): human review of AI claim denials
record.issuing_body: Florida House of Representatives (2026 Regular Session; sponsors Commerce Committee, Insurance & Banking Subcommittee and Rep. Cassel)
record.summary: Would have let workers' compensation carriers, insurers and HMOs use artificial intelligence and machine learning systems to assist in processing claims, but barred them from reducing a claim payment or denying all or part of a claim based solely on such a system's output. A qualified human professional would have had to analyse the claim independently of the system, review the accuracy of its output and make the decision. Carriers would have had to keep records of each such decision, affirm in denial letters that AI was not the sole basis, and describe their AI use and how it complies in their claims-handling manuals.
record.notes: Filed on 24 Nov 2025; committee substitutes were adopted by the Insurance & Banking Subcommittee (9 Dec 2025, which extended the bill to workers' compensation and HMOs) and the Commerce Committee (26 Feb 2026, filed 27 Feb 2026, which dropped references to algorithms). Passed the House 108-0 on 5 Mar 2026, was referred to the Senate Rules Committee and died there on 13 Mar 2026; the Senate bill SB 202 died in Banking and Insurance. The bill stated an effective date of 1 Jul 2026. The Office of Insurance Regulation (insurers and HMOs) and the Department of Financial Services (workers' compensation carriers) would have checked compliance through market conduct examinations, with administrative fines for workers' compensation carriers of up to USD 2,500 per nonwillful and USD 20,000 per willful violation.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for HB 527 (2026) and the House Insurance & Banking Subcommittee (11 Dec 2025) and Commerce Committee (2 Mar 2026) analyses (flsenate.gov). The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, versions (filed, c1, c2 posted 27 Feb 2026), the 108-0 House vote and 'Died in Rules' on 13 Mar 2026; the Commerce analysis covers CS/CS/HB 527, the version the House passed, and the summary rests on it. The bill text itself was not stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: Passed the House 108-0 on 5 Mar 2026, then 'Died in Rules' in the Senate on 13 Mar 2026, the last action. A bill that died at the end of the session is Proposed with status Lapsed; its stated effective date (1 Jul 2026) never applied.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope with no scope_note: a lapsed AI-specific bill that would have required human review of AI-assisted insurance claim denials, with recordkeeping, disclosure and supervisory enforcement. It passed one chamber unanimously, so it is not a bill with little chance of passing.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the filing date (24 Nov 2025), as for the other Florida bills in the register; date_last_updated is the posting of the last version, CS/CS (c2), on 27 Feb 2026, the text the House passed.
judgment.related_reasoning: No existing record is a direct counterpart for AI in insurance claims handling; Colorado's ADMT law (US-CO-02) covers insurance decisions among many others and is not linked.
